p: All 29 non-fallback batch/context cells are analyzed on both ranks: 406 paired-graph cycles. The selected schedule has zero measured target-communication/draft-communication, draft-communication/draft-compute, and target-compute/draft-compute intersections across every captured cycle. The previous schedule has maximum intersections of 0.3233, 0.0088, and 2.8248 ms respectively.

The table averages each rank’s per-cycle median at B16. Compute coverage is draft-compute time intersecting target communication; communication coverage is draft-communication time intersecting target compute. CV measures spacing between successive draft communication groups. CUDA graph-copy helper kernels (memcpy32_post) are excluded consistently from model-kernel compute accounting in both schedules.

These measurements establish wider placement and collision avoidance, not complete hiding of draft latency. The unit of placement remains an indivisible CUDA kernel; splitting a node list cannot preempt a long attention or matrix-multiplication kernel. Phase fences may extend target windows, and NCCL duration includes synchronization waits. The independent verification-A/draft-B pair also excludes the dependent stages elsewhere in the decode iteration.

At B16/128k on rank 0, draft FA3 attention accounts for about 0.971 ms per paired cycle outside target communication; only 1.9% of that kernel class overlaps target communication. Overall draft-compute coverage at B16 declines from 76.4% at 4k to 23.4% at 128k, even though placement spans the timeline. The two long attention kernels visibly extend their phase windows and hold target compute until completion. Full hiding has not been achieved.
